lr_mira_existing_promise.name: Mira
lines: Kael: I have a commitment to Vale. You need to know that before I offer you anything.
Mira: Then you have a conversation to have with her, not an answer to take from me. I won't be the quiet exception to your promise.

actions.label: You're right. I can offer friendship here, nothing concealed.

relationship_event.text: Kael disclosed his commitment to Vale and chose friendship with Mira rather than making a second promise.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Nothing hidden between us. That makes the friendship possible.

lr_vale_existing_promise.name: Vale
lines: Kael: I have made a commitment to Mira. I cannot leave that outside this conversation.
Vale: Then don't. If that promise changes, she should hear it from you. I won't write myself into the space you leave unspoken.

actions.label: Then friendship, without a second promise.

relationship_event.text: Kael disclosed his commitment to Mira and chose friendship with Vale rather than making a second promise.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I'm glad there was no hidden sentence in that answer.

lr_rook_confidence.name: Rook
lines: Rook: A private thing, then. I can manage that.
Kael: No wager?
Rook: Not everything valuable belongs on a table. Terrible discovery. Keep it quiet.

lr_anwen_confidence.name: Anwen
lines: Anwen: I am glad you have someone to return to. Their life is not a reward for what you survived.
Kael: I know.
Anwen: I thought you did. May the ordinary days be kind to you both. I won't make your news the village's.

lr_vale_vulnerable.name: Vale
lr_vale_vulnerable.greeting: I keep listening for the steward to tell me which part of this I am allowed to remember. It is an unpleasant habit to discover in yourself.
lines: Kael: You could leave.
Vale: I could. First I want to put copies where the witnesses can reach them. I don't want to exchange his permission for yours.
Kael: I didn't mean it that way.
Vale: I believe you. I still need to say it.

variants.greeting: The copied facts survived. Hiding the original left me answering questions I didn't choose. I need you to understand both things.

actions.label: Your work and your leaving are yours to choose.

relationship_event.text: Kael acknowledged that Vale chooses her own work and future, without requiring her to abandon the witnesses.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You left the decision with me. I'm not accustomed to how much that matters.

actions.label: I still think staying here is a mistake.

relationship_event.text: Vale held her boundary when Kael questioned her decision to remain for the witnesses.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You can worry about me. You cannot turn that worry into an order.

actions.label: I can be your friend without asking where this leads.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Vale kept their friendship without a romantic promise.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I'm glad the friendship didn't need a destination.

lr_vale_boundary.name: Vale
lr_vale_boundary.greeting: I am staying until the copies are in their hands. We can disagree about the risk. We cannot build a life in which you decide what risks I am allowed.

actions.label: I won't decide for you. I can stay in the conversation without winning it.

relationship_event.text: Kael accepted Vale's stated decision without changing it or demanding agreement. The disagreement remains recorded.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: We still disagreed. You let it be a conversation instead of a command.

actions.label: Then let us leave the romance there. I respect your choice.

relationship_event.text: Kael respected Vale's decision and ended the romantic invitation, leaving friendship possible.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: The answer was difficult. Thank you for not making me defend it again.

lr_vale_commitment.name: Vale
lr_vale_commitment.greeting: I want a future with you in it. Not written for me. Not promised somewhere else as well.
lines: Kael: No seal?
Vale: Our own words. And the right to speak again if the words stop being true.

actions.label: I choose you, freely and exclusively.

relationship_event.text: Vale and Kael explicitly chose a mutual, exclusive adult relationship. Her work remains her own.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I am glad to see you. That is my whole reason this time.

actions.label: I can promise honest friendship, but not a shared life.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined romantic commitment to Vale without withdrawing friendship.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: No debt for the answer. Come back when you want company.

lr_vale_future.name: Vale
lr_vale_future.greeting: The assembly has given its answer. It isn't the end of the work. It means I can finally choose which part is mine.
lines: Kael: And the room with the window?
Vale: Still mine to find. I would like to open it before deciding what comes after.
Kael: And the room with the window?
Vale: I would like to show you when I find it. Today, I would like you to stay beside me.
Kael: Because you want me here?
Vale: Because I want you here.

actions.label: Stay close. Make room for a future neither of us has to dictate.

relationship_event.text: After testimony, Vale invited Kael into a quiet, non-explicit affectionate moment and a freely chosen future.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: The window is still a plan. I'm glad it can be a plan, not an escape.

actions.label: Find your room. I'll be glad to hear how it turns out.

relationship_event.text: Kael supported Vale's freely chosen future without assigning her a home or political role.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I can tell you about an ordinary day now. I'm still getting used to that.

lr_vale_end.name: Vale
lr_vale_end.greeting: We said we would speak again if the words stopped being true. I'm listening.
lines: Vale: Whatever this answer is, it won't rewrite the record, or what we were to each other.

actions.label: I cannot keep our commitment. I'm ending it honestly.

relationship_event.text: Kael ended his commitment to Vale in direct conversation. Their past remains part of the record.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: We do not need to pretend none of it happened. We do need room for what comes next.

lr_vale_letter.name: A letter from Vale
lr_vale_letter.greeting: To whoever is asking after the erased names: before you restore a name to a public page, ask whether its living bearer can safely stand beside it. A truthful record is not an instruction to surrender someone to a guard. - Vale, record keeper

lines.speaker: The letter
lines.text: A space is left for a reply carried with Greyfen's ordinary correspondence. There is no key, seal of passage or evidence attached.

actions.label: Reply: I'll ask whose safety the page changes.

relationship_event.text: Kael replied that a record should consider the living person's safety. No identity or consent was supplied by the letter.

actions.label: Reply: Concealment can shelter the powerful too. Who decides?

relationship_event.text: Kael questioned who gets to decide which names remain private.

actions.label: Keep the letter. Send no reply.

relationship_event.text: Kael kept Vale's letter without answering it.

lr_vale_archive.name: Vale
lr_vale_archive.greeting: A woman asked me to keep her statement, but not her address. Fold that leaf inward. The account stays readable; her door stays her own.
lines: Kael: An omission in a truthful record.
Vale: A boundary supplied by its subject. I used to confuse those with omissions supplied by a lord.
Kael: Does she know the difference?
Vale: She made me read it back. Twice.

variants.greeting: You wrote that you would ask whose safety a page changes. Here is someone who answered: keep her account, not her address.
Your letter asked who decides. In this case, the woman whose account it is. She asked me to keep her words, but not her address.

actions.label: Fold the private address inward; keep the statement open.

relationship_event.text: Kael helped preserve a living witness's private address without hiding her account.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: That folded leaf still keeps the account readable. You understood what she was asking.

actions.label: I still worry about who can demand an omission. Leave it with her instructions.

relationship_event.text: Kael questioned omissions while leaving the witness's own instructions intact.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Your question belongs in this room. So does her right to answer it.

actions.label: This is between her and you. I won't handle it.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined to handle the private leaf. Vale preserved it as instructed.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I kept her instructions. You weren't obliged to take that work from me.

lr_vale_personal.name: Vale
lr_vale_personal.greeting: A room with a window I can open myself. That sounds smaller aloud than it did in my head.
lines: Kael: Not from this side of the wall.
Vale: And work I chose, with people who can tell me no. I spent years being useful to the wrong silence.
Kael: Is there room in that picture for company?
Vale: There could be. But I won't mistake someone needing a ledger for someone wanting to know me.

actions.label: I want to know you, not what you can open for me.

relationship_event.text: After direct acquaintance, Kael expressed adult romantic interest in Vale. She welcomed the question without making a commitment.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I'm glad you asked about the window. I wanted someone to understand that part.

actions.label: Then let me be someone you can call a friend.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Vale explicitly chose friendship, independent of the archive.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: A friend is welcome here without bringing a request.

actions.label: I can't offer that kind of company. I won't imply otherwise.

relationship_event.text: Kael respectfully declined a personal relationship with Vale.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Thank you for speaking plainly. The record is still yours to read.

lr_mira_truth_talk.name: Mira
lr_mira_truth_talk.greeting: I would like a life with you in it. But not one where we call a dangerous secret kindness because it keeps our supper quiet.
lines: Kael: You kept a secret to keep people alive.
Mira: I did. And I have to answer for it. Privacy is not a licence to let the next household suffer.
Kael: You want a promise.
Mira: An answer. If we disagree, say so. The medicines are still here either way.

actions.label: No comfort bought by making someone else carry the danger.

relationship_event.text: Kael agreed that a shared life cannot rest on passing a concealed danger to others.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I heard your answer. I will have to live by it as well.

actions.label: Sometimes keeping a dangerous truth quiet is the only mercy left.

relationship_event.text: Mira declined commitment while Kael defended concealing risks. An apology alone does not settle the disagreement.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I care about you. I still cannot build a home on that answer.

actions.label: Let us keep the friendship, without a promise of more.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Mira kept their friendship without entering a romantic commitment.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: A friend can disagree with me. You haven't lost your place here.

lr_mira_boundary.name: Mira
lr_mira_boundary.greeting: I heard the apology. I need to see who gets protected when the next hard choice comes. That isn't work I can do for you.
lines: Kael: And until then?
Mira: We can talk. We can be kind. We cannot pretend the question went away.

actions.label: Then friendship, without asking you to wait for me.

relationship_event.text: Kael respected Mira's boundary and chose friendship without asking her to wait.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You didn't ask me to wait for a different answer. Thank you.

lr_mira_reconcile.name: Mira
lr_mira_reconcile.greeting: You have done more than say you were sorry. A dangerous account is no longer being kept at someone else's expense.
lines: Kael: It doesn't make the first answer right.
Mira: No. It gives me something besides that answer to trust. I would like to try again, slowly.

actions.label: Slowly. And without pretending it never happened.

relationship_event.text: After consequential care and preserved truth, Mira and Kael reopened their personal conversation. The disagreement remains in their history.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: We didn't erase the argument. We found a way to talk after it.

actions.label: I would rather keep the friendship we have.

relationship_event.text: Kael chose friendship after reconciliation.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Then friends. There is plenty in that word.

lr_mira_commitment.name: Mira
lr_mira_commitment.greeting: I want you in my life, Kael. Not as a debt for help, and not as a visitor who promises every door the same return.
lines: Kael: And the work here?
Mira: Mine to choose. I am not asking you to carry me away from it. I'm asking whether we choose each other.

actions.label: I choose you. No other commitment left unspoken.

relationship_event.text: Mira and Kael explicitly chose a mutual, exclusive adult relationship.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You came back. I was hoping for that, not counting it as something owed.

actions.label: I can offer friendship honestly, not that promise.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined commitment to Mira and offered friendship plainly.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You gave me an honest answer. We can start the next conversation from there.

lr_mira_quiet.name: Mira
lr_mira_quiet.greeting: The last patient is resting. I can put this basket down now.
lines: Kael: Shall I stay?
Mira: Yes. Because I want you here.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Come closer. No account to settle for a moment.
lines.direction: An unhurried invitation; no forced body contact or camera cut.

actions.label: Stay with her in the quiet.

relationship_event.text: Mira and Kael shared a private, non-explicit affectionate moment by mutual invitation.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I keep finding time for those quiet minutes. It seems I want to.

lr_mira_end.name: Mira
lr_mira_end.greeting: Then say it plainly. I would rather hear the truth here than find it in somebody else's kindness.
lines: Mira: Ending this doesn't undo what was good. It doesn't change who needs medicine either.

actions.label: I cannot keep our commitment. I'm ending it, not asking you to wait.

relationship_event.text: Kael ended his commitment to Mira in a direct conversation. The past relationship is preserved in the record.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: We said what needed saying. Give it room. The medicines are here, as always.

lr_mira_garden_offer.name: Mira
lr_mira_garden_offer.greeting: The damp stems need separating before they spoil the rest. Ordinary work. No one gets a song for it.
lines: Kael: Perhaps a very short song.
Mira: You can make it up by the beds. Keep the dry bundles apart. Those are for the houses, not the shop.

actions.label: I'll sort them.
actions.result: Sort the drying stems beside Mira's herb beds.

actions.label: Not today. I won't promise time I don't have.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined garden work without promising to return.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I found time for the stems. You can still sit down, Kael. Work isn't the price of company.

lr_mira_garden_done.name: Mira
lr_mira_garden_done.greeting: Those will keep. Thank you. Most people offer to kill something when I ask for help.
lines: Kael: I know a useful knot as well.
Mira: An alarming range of talents. Leave the bundles here. I'll take them round when the fever breaks.

actions.label: I'll leave you to it. Keep me a little company next time.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Mira shared ordinary garden work. Neither made a romantic promise.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: No damp stems today. Sit for a moment; I can spare that much.

lr_mira_supplies.name: Mira
lr_mira_supplies.greeting: One fever easing. One getting worse. Reports settle an account, not a bedside.
lines: Kael: Do you ever leave the work?
Mira: Sometimes. Not because someone decides I have done enough for them.
Kael: I wasn't asking you to leave.
Mira: Good. Then ask me what I need, not when I'll be finished.

actions.label: What do you need?
actions.result: Clean water, sound bundles and room to work. Kael listens without making a new delivery promise.

relationship_event.text: Kael asked about Mira's patients and respected that her work was her own.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You asked what I needed instead of telling me to rest. I remember that.

actions.label: Then I'll give you room to work.

relationship_event.text: Kael gave Mira room to attend to her patients.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: The patient is resting. Thank you for not making me choose between work and politeness.

lr_mira_personal.name: Mira
lr_mira_personal.greeting: You know what fed those roots now. I won't pretend being kind to me makes that knowledge easier.
lines: Kael: I didn't come to weigh you again.
Mira: Then stay a moment. Tell me something small.
Kael: I used to think a quiet house meant everyone had left.
Mira: Mine is quiet for perhaps ten minutes a day. I've grown rather fond of it.
Kael: I'd like to know those minutes.
Mira: As a friend, or something you should ask plainly?

actions.label: Something more, if you want that too. No promise owed.
actions.result: Mira wants time to know Kael outside an emergency. Interest is mutual; commitment is not yet offered.

relationship_event.text: Kael offered adult romantic interest. Mira welcomed another conversation, not an automatic relationship.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I haven't forgotten what you asked. I want a little ordinary time with you before we promise anything.

actions.label: A friend. That's not a smaller thing.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Mira chose friendship explicitly.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: There's a place here for my friend. No other meaning hidden in it.

actions.label: I'm not ready to ask either of us for more.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined a closer relationship without changing Mira's medical, evidence or testimony obligations.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: No unfinished question between us. Tell me about the road, when you're ready.

lr_rook_stool_offer.name: Rook
lr_rook_stool_offer.greeting: Lost that leg at Three Marks. Well, lost the money for the carpenter. The leg followed out of sympathy.
lines: Kael: You could stop wagering the furniture.
Rook: And leave the roof undefended? Brace the stool by the common table. I've a peg that almost fits.

actions.label: I'll brace it.
actions.result: Rook leaves the loose stool beside the common table for Kael to brace.

actions.label: Not today. Keep the roof.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined to help repair the common-table stool.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: I found another brace for the stool. No debt between us. A game, perhaps.

lr_rook_stool_done.name: Rook
lr_rook_stool_done.greeting: Solid. There goes my last excuse for losing.
lines: Kael: The cards were marked?
Rook: Stones. And no. I'm trying honesty. It leaves a man terribly exposed.
Kael: At least he'll stay seated.

actions.label: Save me a place at the table.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Rook repaired the stool and agreed to share the common table again.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Your seat's still there. I haven't wagered it. Yet.

lr_tor_hinge_offer.name: Tor
lr_tor_hinge_offer.greeting: Hold this flat while I seat the pin. Elna's door has been announcing her business to the whole street.
lines: Kael: No mark on it?
Tor: A hinge doesn't need my name. It needs to open when her hands are full.

actions.label: I'll hold it at the bench.
actions.result: The hinge waits at the forge bench, beside Tor's stock.

actions.label: I have to get back to the road.

relationship_event.text: Kael declined the hinge repair. Tor's shop and ordinary help remain available.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Managed the hinge with a clamp. Road still keeping you?

lr_tor_hinge_done.name: Tor
lines: Kael: Nothing.
Tor: Best thing a door can say.
Kael: You won't see it again.
Tor: I'll see her carrying the wash through it. That's enough.

actions.label: Good work, then.

relationship_event.text: Kael helped Tor fit a household hinge and shared a quiet moment about useful work.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Elna carried the wash through without putting the basket down. Our hinge did its work.

lr_anwen_shrine_offer.name: Anwen
lr_anwen_shrine_offer.greeting: The cloths need folding. Leave the names where they are. I have moved enough things out of sight.
lines: Kael: You don't have to explain every fold.
Anwen: No. But I am learning which things I do have to explain.

actions.label: I'll put the cloths in order at the shrine.
actions.result: The loose cloths wait by the shrine bench. The recorded names are not to be moved.

actions.label: I need some distance first.

relationship_event.text: Kael asked for distance after the report. He did not offer reconciliation.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You asked for room. The work here doesn't make you owe me forgiveness.

lr_anwen_shrine_done.name: Anwen
lr_anwen_shrine_done.greeting: It is easier to keep a table than an account. I used to pretend they were the same work.
lines: Kael: The names are still here.
Anwen: Yes. Whatever you think of me, they stay.

actions.label: You can keep doing the work now.

relationship_event.text: Kael helped tidy the shrine and encouraged Anwen to keep doing the work, without erasing her responsibility.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You said to keep doing the work. I'm here.

actions.label: Care doesn't make concealing those names right.

relationship_event.text: Kael helped with the shrine while explicitly challenging Anwen's concealment. Help did not mean absolution.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: You were right: a clean cloth does not answer for a hidden name. I remember both things you did here.

actions.label: Stay beside her in silence.

relationship_event.text: Kael and Anwen shared silence after tidying the shrine. Neither made a promise of forgiveness.
relationship_event.acknowledgement: Thank you for the quiet. I won't put words in it.

opening_care_invitation.name: Anwen
opening_care_invitation.greeting: A moment, hunter. The man behind that screen cannot reach his water.
lines: Anwen: The cup is on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.
Anwen: And that little coat on the bench belongs under the shelf. Oren will complain if I let the rain into his pockets.

variants.greeting: Thank you for the water. He has stopped trying to stand.
lines: Anwen: Would you move that little coat under the shelf? Oren left it here this morning. He said he would be too hot.

variants.greeting: You found a dry place for his coat. Thank you.
lines: Anwen: The man behind the screen needs the cup on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.

actions.label: I'll help here for a moment.
Tell me about the missing travelers.

opening_care_water.name: Anwen
opening_care_water.greeting: There. Close enough that he need not ask again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A hand comes beneath the screen. It steadies the cup against the wood before lifting it.

lines: Kael: Was he with the missing cart?
Anwen: No. A fall on the south road. Not every hurt here is a sign, Kael. Some people only need water.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cup comes back to the linen. For a moment, the breathing behind the screen is easier.

opening_care_coat.name: Anwen
opening_care_coat.greeting: That is Oren's. Leave the pockets turned in; he keeps things in them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The small coat is heavier at one cuff. Three crooked red stitches hold a tear shut. Kael folds the sleeve beneath it, clear of the wet edge.

lines: Kael: Did you mend this?
Anwen: He did. I threaded the needle. He would not let me do the rest.
Anwen: Bram drove the cart. Sella took Oren beside her. He left this because the sun was out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Anwen leaves room on the bench beside the coat. She has not put it away.

soldiers_stand_down.name: The soldiers at the road
soldiers_stand_down.greeting: The nearest soldier lets his sword point fall into the mud. The other watches Senn before doing the same.
lines: Soldier: He said Greyfen would leave us hungry if we stopped taking what passed.
Kael: I cannot promise nobody will ask what you took. I can promise supper is not a reward for obeying him.
Soldier: And if we speak?
Kael: Then you speak for yourselves. Lowering a weapon does not sign your name to anyone else's account.
The road clears. Senn remains beside the table, without a line of men between his answers and the people he hurt.

work_cart_finish.name: Rook
work_cart_finish.greeting: Mind the corner. That sack has already had a worse journey than either of us.
lines: Kael: The wheel will need lifting before it can turn.
Rook: It will. The flour needed feeding to people before it needed feeding to mud.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A woman at the kitchen opens the sack and measures three small shares. She keeps the string for mending.

lines: Rook: There. Something went where we said it would. I could get used to that.

work_cart_return.name: Rook
work_cart_return.greeting: The kitchen has the flour. The cart is lighter.
lines: Rook: I've told them you did the heavy bit. Don't make me a liar by offering to do it all again.

work_road_finish.name: Tor
work_road_finish.greeting: Leave the peg proud. Someone will need to pull it out when the next flood comes.
lines: Kael: You expect it to fail?
Tor: I expect someone to repair it. A thing can be well made without being the last thing anyone ever makes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Water threads through the cleared drain. Rook's empty wheel crosses the boards without sinking.

lines: Tor: There. A road ought to carry the person using it. Start with that.

work_road_return.name: Tor
work_road_return.greeting: Water's still moving. Boards are still holding.
lines: Tor: If you're looking for praise, ask the wheel. It made the most noise about it before.

work_relief_finish.name: The common kitchen
work_relief_finish.greeting: The two empty baskets return together.
lines: Mira: Did anyone ask what they had to promise?
Kael: One woman did.
Mira: And?
Kael: I told her the basket was not a contract.
Mira: Tell her again tomorrow. People don't learn that sort of thing in one meal.

work_relief_return.name: The common kitchen
work_relief_return.greeting: The household shares have been delivered.
lines: Names in the ledger mark who has eaten. They do not mark who owes obedience.

aftermath_names_witness.name: Anwen
aftermath_names_witness.greeting: I thought writing them where everyone could see would make my hands stop shaking.
lines: Kael: It made you begin.
Anwen: Bram. Sella. Oren. I have practiced saying the names of the dead more often than I have spoken to the people who miss them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A man waiting at the wall asks who will pay for the land his mother was refused. Anwen puts his question beneath the names instead of sending him away.

lines: Anwen: We cannot promise every answer today.
Kael: We can promise this question will still be here tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Anwen leaves room on the board. The public account is no longer a ceremony that ends when the bell stops.

lines: Anwen: Tor has begun measuring timber. Rook is arguing about who gets the first load. Go help them make this more than my handwriting.

aftermath_names_mercy.name: Anwen
aftermath_names_mercy.greeting: This copy names the offices, the orders and those who gave them. This other book belongs to the families.
lines: Kael: Who can open it?
Anwen: The people whose lives it holds. They may let someone else read. They may refuse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A woman returns a sealed page. She asks Anwen to keep her son's name and destroy the account of his last fear. Anwen asks once whether she is certain, then follows her instruction.

lines: Kael: Edric's order stays on the wall.
Anwen: Yes. His privacy was never the thing we were protecting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time, the bell can mourn someone without claiming everything that happened to them.

lines: Anwen: The living still need timber and flour. Tor is at the bench. There is a world outside these books.

aftermath_names_duty.name: Anwen
aftermath_names_duty.greeting: The silence held through the night. I kept waking to make sure.
lines: Kael: I felt the road when I woke. Not words. Weight.
Anwen: Then we write the limits now, while people are grateful enough to forget them. You did not accept every order anyone might give you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She writes that the keeping is Kael's choice. No child inherits it. No shortage can compel another keeper. The old command remains beside it, uncensored.

lines: Kael: If I cannot keep it?
Anwen: We meet again. We tell the truth about the cost. We do not turn your promise into an excuse to stop thinking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Kael reads the lines before signing. The tremor in his hand is his own.

lines: Anwen: Tor has a repair for you. Something ordinary. Let him do it.

aftermath_names_ash.name: Anwen
aftermath_names_ash.greeting: Nothing answered when I rang the bell.
lines: Kael: Were you hoping it would?
Anwen: I don't know. That is the honest answer today.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The copied command and the household register lie on her table. Human hands saved them before the glade burned. Their evidence has not become less true because its witness is gone.

lines: Anwen: There are things we can no longer ask. We must mark those gaps instead of filling them with convenient answers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A father passing the table says his child slept without hearing voices. Anwen listens until he has finished.

lines: Kael: We keep what remains. And answer for what we chose.
Anwen: Tor needs another pair of hands. The next repair cannot wait for us to feel certain.

aftermath_work_witness.name: Tor and Rook
aftermath_work_witness.greeting: Tor lays a damaged hinge on the bench. Rook lays three incompatible requests beside it.
lines: Rook: The west field wants its gate. The kitchen wants its cart. The chapel wants a board large enough to accuse the whole county.
Tor: The chapel can have the offcuts.
Kael holds the hinge while Tor drives out its old pin. The iron bears the same stamp as the weapon that brought him here.
Kael: Who decides whose repair comes first?
Rook: Today? The people standing here. Tomorrow we'll need something better than whoever shouts loudest.
Tor: Put that on Anwen's board.
The first repair is small enough to finish. Beyond it lies work no ending could have finished for them.

aftermath_work_mercy.name: Tor and Rook
aftermath_work_mercy.greeting: Rook has tied a strip of plain linen around a basket with no name on it.
lines: Kael: Where does that go?
Rook: To someone who asked me not to tell everyone where it goes.
Tor: You can still count the flour without counting the family's grief.
Kael steadies a plank against Tor's bench. Together they cut a lid for the basket; Rook folds the linen beneath it so the rain cannot reach the meal.
Rook: Keeping a confidence used to mean hiding my own part. I'll have to learn the difference.
Kael: Ask whose safety the silence serves.
Rook takes the basket through the square openly. Its destination remains the recipient's business.

aftermath_work_duty.name: Tor and Rook
aftermath_work_duty.greeting: Tor reaches for Kael's worn strap before asking about the glade.
lines: Tor: Sit. If you're going to stand watch, you can at least stop this buckle cutting your shoulder.
Kael: There are other repairs.
Tor: This is one of them.
Rook lays out the roads that still need walking. He marks a place for Kael to rest and a name beside each delivery. None of those names is entered as a new keeper.
Rook: Help isn't the same thing as taking your oath. We can carry supper without carrying the Hart.
Kael holds the leather while Tor stitches. For a little while, his chosen burden fits beside someone else's ordinary skill.
Tor: Come back before it splits again. That is a request, not a sacred duty.

aftermath_work_ash.name: Tor and Rook
aftermath_work_ash.greeting: There is ash in the grain sack's folded seam. Rook brushes it into his palm before opening the flour.
lines: Rook: It got everywhere. Doesn't mean everything is ruined.
Tor: No. Doesn't mean it didn't cost anything either.
Kael helps separate the scorched boards from the sound ones. One will become a shelf. Another breaks under his hand and is set aside.
Kael: I cannot put it back.
Tor: I didn't ask you to. Hold this end.
They finish one repair without deciding what the whole choice meant. In the kitchen, someone laughs at an ordinary mistake.
Rook: Listen. I missed that. We can miss what was lost and still be glad to hear it.

aftermath_road_witness.name: The road beyond Greyfen
aftermath_road_witness.greeting: The notice at the village edge carries the first names, the first claims, and a time for the next meeting.
lines: Kael: A public promise has a place people can return to.
Some will come to demand restitution. Some will come to defend what they have. The account will need witnesses after the extraordinary witness is gone.
Rook: Will you be here when they arrive?
Kael: I said I would keep it.
He takes the road back toward the kitchen. This time, returning is part of the oath.
Your campaign outcome is kept. Greyfen and the discovered roads remain open for unfinished conversations and work.

aftermath_road_mercy.name: The road beyond Greyfen
aftermath_road_mercy.greeting: A strip of linen moves beside the road. It carries no confession and names no debtor.
lines: Kael: They asked for a marker. Nothing more.
Rook: Then it can be nothing more.

The released memories do not arrive to correct the village's version of itself. People must preserve the records, challenge the convenient lie, and let one another keep what was never owed to a crowd.
Kael turns toward the kitchen. There are names he will speak there, and names he will wait to be invited to speak.
No one mistakes the work ahead for permission to bind the dead again.
Your campaign outcome is kept. Greyfen and the discovered roads remain open for unfinished conversations and work.

aftermath_road_duty.name: The road beyond Greyfen
aftermath_road_duty.greeting: At the village edge, Kael feels where the old road bends even with his eyes closed.
lines: Rook: How far does it follow you?
Kael: I will have to learn.
Rook: Then don't answer for all the years today.
The boundary is quieter. The injustice it covered has not been repaired by one man's willingness to stand here. The written account waits in Greyfen, where other people can begin their own work.
Kael opens his eyes. His oath has limits. His life must still have room inside them.
Your campaign outcome is kept. Greyfen and the discovered roads remain open for unfinished conversations and work.

aftermath_road_ash.name: The road beyond Greyfen
aftermath_road_ash.greeting: Wind crosses the road without forming a voice. A patch of earth where oathgrass grew is bare.
lines: Kael kneels and presses a seed into the ordinary soil. He cannot make it take root by promising.
Rook: Will it grow?
Kael: We can water it. We can come back.
The destroyed witness cannot answer the questions no one thought to ask. The human record can still accuse the powerful. The living can still choose what they owe each other.
Kael stands. The quiet is relief, and it is absence. He carries both toward Greyfen.
Your campaign outcome is kept. Greyfen and the discovered roads remain open for unfinished conversations and work.
